operational_model: Each block freezes planned slot IDs, deadline, and B_cap before slot outcomes.
The monitor persists an ordered journal of closed {predictable_weight, block_score} summaries plus at most one active block.
Recovery rebuilds V3 by replaying closed summaries in order; V3 root caches are not scientific durable state.
If recovery occurs after the frozen active-block deadline, the active block closes immediately with every missing slot scored one.
Events arriving during simulated downtime are not retroactively recovered; they remain operational no-result and therefore fail closed.
Duplicate and late deliveries are rejected rather than replacing a previously accepted or failed planned-slot outcome.
conclusion: Across the tested multi-block crash/restart campaigns, journal replay reproduced the uninterrupted durable post-recovery V3 endpoint exactly at all 1,440 checks and produced no threshold-decision or state-roundtrip mismatch.
scope_guards: This validates deterministic replay/state-machine behavior under the tested crash model; it is not a proof against storage corruption or adversarial journal tampering.

The operational outage model intentionally changes which canonical results are available; equality is required between persisted/recovered execution and a direct execution under the same availability history, not against a hypothetical no-outage run.
Replay correctness does not strengthen the underlying V3 confidence-sequence theorem.
